steps.message:
Build a 9-slide, 16:9 PowerPoint presentation titled "Global CO₂ Emissions: Trends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities" for policy analysts and climate negotiators, using a data-forward, analytical, and authoritative tone.

The deck opens with a striking title slide establishing scope (1750–2024), then builds from the atmospheric CO₂ milestone through historical emission growth, national comparisons, and regional share shifts. It deepens into per capita inequalities and the 2024 annual change snapshot, before explaining how energy mix drives differences and closing with key takeaways that synthesize the findings.

For the per capita slide (slide 6), use a horizontal bar chart layout showing emissions for the US, Canada, China, EU-27, World average, UK, India, and Chad/Kenya to emphasize the 150× disparity. For the energy mix slide (slide 8), include a small comparison table contrasting France/UK versus Germany/Netherlands on energy sources and per capita CO₂. The regional share shift slide (slide 5) should describe a stacked area or side-by-side comparison visual showing the dramatic change from 1900 to 2024. Reference the appropriate figures (figure_1.jpg through figure_4.jpg) as noted in the slide specifications.

Do not fabricate any data not found in source_brief.md. All statistics, figures, and claims must be grounded in the provided source material.


## Data Sources

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

arguments.command:
cat << 'EOF' > generate_ppt.py
import collections
import collections.abc
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_LEGEND_POSITION
import os

prs = Presentation()
# Set 16:9 aspect ratio
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Helper function to add title
def add_title(slide, text):
    title = slide.shapes.title
    title.text = text
    title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(36)
    title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
    title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0, 51, 102)

# --- Slide 1: Title Slide ---
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0] # Title slide
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
title = slide.shapes.title
subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
title.text = "Global CO₂ Emissions:\nTrends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities"
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0, 51, 102)
subtitle.text = "A data-driven overview from 1750 to 2024\n\nData Sources: Global Carbon Budget 2025, NASA"

# --- Slide 2: Atmospheric CO2 ---
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5]) # Title only
add_title(slide, "Atmospheric CO₂ Reaches 429 ppm — 50% Above Pre-Industrial Levels")

txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(11), Inches(2))
tf = txBox.text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Latest Measurement (Feb 2026): 429 ppm"
p.font.size = Pt(32)
p.font.bold = True
p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(204, 0, 0)

p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
p2.text = "• Pre-industrial baseline: ~280 ppm\n• A more than 50% increase, accelerating sharply since 1958\n• 1.5× greater than the natural increase at the end of the last ice age (which took thousands of years)"
p2.font.size = Pt(24)

# --- Slide 3: Global Emissions Trajectory ---
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
add_title(slide, "Global Fossil Fuel CO₂ Emissions Grew Six-Fold: 6 Billion to 35+ Billion Tonnes")

txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(1.5), Inches(11), Inches(1))
tf = txBox.text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "From negligible levels in 1750, emissions hit 6 Bt in 1950, 20 Bt in 1990, and exceed 35 Bt today."
p.font.size = Pt(20)

chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ['1750', '1950', '1990', '2024']
chart_data.add_series('Global Emissions (Billion tonnes)', (0.1, 6, 20, 35.5))

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2.5), Inches(11), Inches(4.5)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
    XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
).chart
chart.has_legend = True
chart.legend.position = XL_LEGEND_POSITION.BOTTOM
chart.value_axis.has_title = True
chart.value_axis.axis_title.text_frame.text = "Billion Tonnes CO₂"

# --- Slide 4: Who Emits the Most? ---
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
add_title(slide, "China Now Emits Over 12 Billion Tonnes — More Than Double the United States")

# Table
rows, cols = 8, 4
x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(6), Inches(4)
shape = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, x, y, cx, cy)
table = shape.table

data = [
    ["Country / Region", "Annual CO₂ (Bt)", "Share", "Trend"],
    ["China", "~12.5", "~27%", "Slight increase"],
    ["United States", "~5.0", "~14%", "Declining"],
    ["India", "~3.0", "~8%", "Rising"],
    ["EU-27", "~2.7", "~7%", "Declining"],
    ["Germany", "~0.6", "~1.7%", "Declining"],
    ["Brazil", "~0.5", "~1.4%", "Stable"],
    ["France / UK", "~0.3 (each)", "~0.8-0.9%", "Declining"]
]

for row_idx, row in enumerate(data):
    for col_idx, val in enumerate(row):
        cell = table.cell(row_idx, col_idx)
        cell.text = val
        cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(14)
        if row_idx == 0:
            cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True

if os.path.exists('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_3.jpg'):
    slide.shapes.add_picture('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_3.jpg', Inches(7), Inches(2), width=Inches(6))

# --- Slide 5: Regional Share Shift ---
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
add_title(slide, "Asia Now Accounts for ~50% of Global Emissions; US + Europe Below One-Third")

txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(1.5), Inches(11), Inches(1))
tf = txBox.text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "In 1900, Europe and the US dominated (>90%). Today, Asia leads (~50%), while Africa and South America each remain at just 3-4%."
p.font.size = Pt(20)

chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ['1900', '1950', '2024']
chart_data.add_series('US + Europe', (91, 85, 32))
chart_data.add_series('Asia', (5, 8, 50))
chart_data.add_series('Africa + South America', (2, 4, 8))
chart_data.add_series('Others', (2, 3, 10))

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2.5), Inches(11), Inches(4.5)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_STACKED_100, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
).chart
chart.has_legend = True
chart.legend.position = XL_LEGEND_POSITION.RIGHT

# --- Slide 6: Per Capita Gap ---
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
add_title(slide, "Per Capita Gap: 15 t in the US vs. 0.1 t in Chad — a 150× Disparity")

if os.path.exists('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_1.jpg'):
    slide.shapes.add_picture('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_1.jpg', Inches(7.5), Inches(2.5), width=Inches(5))

chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ['US', 'Canada', 'China', 'EU-27', 'World Avg', 'UK', 'India', 'Chad/Kenya']
# Values
values = [15, 13, 9, 7, 5, 4, 2, 0.1]
chart_data.add_series('Tonnes per year', values)

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(6.5), Inches(5.5)
chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
    XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
).chart
chart.has_legend = False
chart.value_axis.has_title = True
chart.value_axis.axis_title.text_frame.text = "Tonnes CO₂ / person"


# --- Slide 7: 2024 Snapshot ---
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
add_title(slide, "2024 Snapshot: US and Europe Cut Emissions While Russia and SE Asia Increase")

txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(12), Inches(1))
tf = txBox.text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• US and much of Europe: Declines of roughly -1% to -5%\n• Russia, SE Asia, and parts of Africa: Increases of +2% to +10% or more"
p.font.size = Pt(20)

if os.path.exists('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_4.jpg'):
    slide.shapes.add_picture('/app/benchmark/assets/figure_4.jpg', Inches(2), Inches(2.5), height=Inches(4.5))

# --- Slide 8: Energy Mix ---
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
add_title(slide, "Energy Mix Explains Why France Emits Far Less Per Capita Than Germany")

txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(1.5), Inches(11), Inches(1.5))
tf = txBox.text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Countries with similar living standards can differ significantly based on their energy mix. France and the UK have much lower per capita emissions than Germany or the Netherlands due to higher nuclear and renewable shares."
p.font.size = Pt(22)

# Table
rows, cols = 3, 3
x, y, cx, cy = Inches(2), Inches(3.5), Inches(9), Inches(2)
shape = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, x, y, cx, cy)
table = shape.table
table.columns[0].width = Inches(3)
table.columns[1].width = Inches(2)
table.columns[2].width = Inches(4)

data = [
    ["Region / Country", "Per Capita CO₂", "Primary Energy Driver"],
    ["France / UK", "~4 tonnes/year", "Higher nuclear & renewable shares"],
    ["Germany / Netherlands", "Higher (above EU avg)", "Higher fossil fuel share"]
]

for row_idx, row in enumerate(data):
    for col_idx, val in enumerate(row):
        cell = table.cell(row_idx, col_idx)
        cell.text = val
        cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(18)
        if row_idx == 0:
            cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True

# --- Slide 9: Key Takeaways ---
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
add_title(slide, "Key Takeaways: Emissions Are Still Rising, But the Map of Responsibility Is Shifting")

txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(1.5), Inches(11), Inches(5))
tf = txBox.text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True

points = [
    "Global emissions exceed 35 Bt and have not yet peaked, despite slowing growth.",
    "China alone emits >25% of the global total, more than double the United States.",
    "Per capita inequalities remain extreme, with a 150× gap between the highest emitters and the lowest.",
    "The US and Europe are seeing declining emissions, though their historical cumulative responsibility remains large.",
    "Policy choices matter: energy mix (renewables, nuclear vs. fossil fuels) largely determines per capita outcomes among developed nations."
]

for pt in points:
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.text = "• " + pt
    p.font.size = Pt(24)
    p.space_before = Pt(14)

os.makedirs('/app/output', exist_ok=True)
prs.save('/app/output/final_deck.pptx')
EOF
